def reference(values):
    # Obviously-correct model: keep integers but NOT booleans,
    # since True/False are not "integers" conceptually even though
    # isinstance(True, int) is True in Python.
    return [x for x in values if isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool)]

@given(st.lists(_any_value, max_size=20))
def test_result_is_subsequence_preserving_order(vals):
    result = filter_integers(vals)
    # every result element must appear in order in the input
    idx = 0
    for v in vals:
        if idx < len(result) and v is result[idx] or (idx < len(result) and type(v) is int and v == result[idx] and type(v) == type(result[idx])):
            # need careful walk: advance when types match exactly
            pass
        else:
            continue
    # simpler robust check: reference equality of filtered sequence
    assert result == reference(vals)
    # order check: indices strictly increasing
    positions = []
    start = 0
    for r in result:
        found = None
        for i in range(start, len(vals)):
            if type(vals[i]) is int and vals[i] == r and type(vals[i]) == type(r):
                # type is int covers value equality; bool already excluded
                found = i
                break
            if isinstance(vals[i], int) and not isinstance(vals[i], bool) and vals[i] == r:
                found = i
                break
        assert found is not None
        positions.append(found)
        start = found + 1
    assert positions == sorted(positions)
